item.meaning: A voluntary enterprise democratically owned and managed by producers to process and sell goods without middlemen.

item.definition: The economic sector comprising activities that directly extract raw materials and natural resources from the environment.
The economic sector responsible for manufacturing, construction, and processing raw materials into finished goods.
The service sector providing administrative, transport, commercial, financial, and logistics support to other sectors.

item.title: Interdependence of Economic Sectors
item.explanation: Primary raw material extraction, secondary manufacturing, and tertiary services form a continuous supply chain where no single sector can function alone.

item.statement: Recycling 1 tonne of paper saves 17 trees, 2.5 cubic metres of landfill space, and reduces energy and water consumption by 70%.

item.name: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
item.role_or_contribution: Freedom fighter and leader who advised Anand dairy farmers in the 1940s to form a cooperative to eliminate middlemen exploitation.

item.name: Tribhuvandas Patel
item.role_or_contribution: Social leader who co-founded the AMUL dairy cooperative movement in Anand, Gujarat in 1946.

item.name: Dr. Verghese Kurien
item.role_or_contribution: Engineer known as the 'Father of the White Revolution' in India who led the expansion and technological growth of AMUL.

item.name: Kauṭilya (Chanakya)
item.role_or_contribution: Ancient Indian scholar and statesman whose treatise Arthaśhāstra states: 'The root of prosperity is economic activity'.

item.name: Anand
item.significance: City in Gujarat where the historic AMUL dairy cooperative movement originated in 1946.

item.historical_significance: Formation of Kaira District Co-operative Milk Producers' Union in Anand, eliminating middlemen and empowering dairy farmers.

item.name: AMUL Dairy Cooperative
item.function: A democratic producer cooperative empowering small dairy farmers in Gujarat by collectively processing, pasteurising, and marketing milk.

stages: 1. Primary Stage: Forestry workers harvest timber trees and extract wood pulp from forests.
2. Secondary Stage (Paper Mill): Industrial workers process pulp into large paper rolls.
3. Secondary Stage (Printing Press): Printers bind text and images onto paper to assemble textbooks.
4. Tertiary Stage (Logistics & Distribution): Transport trucks deliver books to warehouses and retail stores.
5. Tertiary Stage (Retail): Bookstores sell finished textbooks directly to students.

item.cause: Lack of refrigeration and perishable nature of raw milk in 1940s Anand
item.effect: Milk farmers were forced to sell to private middlemen at unfair low prices, prompting the creation of the AMUL cooperative.

items: 1. Primary Sector: Natural resource extraction (farming, fishing, mining, forestry).
2. Secondary Sector: Manufacturing, utilities, and construction (factories, mills, power plants).
3. Tertiary Sector: Services, logistics, banking, trade, and retail.

item.description: Democratic organizations of primary producers that process and market goods directly to eliminate middleman exploitation.
The environmental and financial savings achieved by reprocessing waste materials (e.g., paper, water) back into production cycles.
